# Study overview

[Finkelstein et al. (2012)](https://doi.org/10.1093/qje/qjs020) used Oregon's
Medicaid lottery to study insurance coverage. The first-year study found
increased healthcare use and reduced financial strain, but no statistically
significant survival improvement. Here lottery selection instruments Medicaid
enrollment to estimate death-risk effects among enrollment compliers. The
74,922-person public cohort lacks the required lottery-list household-size
control, so this is an exploratory public-data comparison, not an exact
replication. The [paper](Finkelstein_2012.pdf) is retained locally.

# Dataset

```{r load-data}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(ivreg)
  library(sandwich)
  library(princeBART)
  library(future)
  library(posterior)
})

load("processed_data.rda")
head(dat, 5)
```

- **Outcome (`postn_death`):** death after matched lottery notification during 2008--2009.
- **Treatment (`ohp_all_ever_matchn_30sep2009`):** any Medicaid enrollment between matched notification and
  September 30, 2009.
- **Instrument (`treatment`):** lottery selection.
- **Covariates:** lottery draw, phone-number provision, PO-box address,
  self-registration, and signup week. Identifiers are not predictors.

# Objective 1: Death risk among Medicaid-enrollment compliers

## 2SLS analysis

Adjust for the available baseline predictors and cluster standard errors by
household. The missing household-size adjustment remains an identification
limitation; the additional predictors do not replace it.

```{r two-stage-least-squares}
fit_iv <- ivreg(
  postn_death ~ ohp_all_ever_matchn_30sep2009 + draw_lottery + have_phone_list + pobox_list + self_list + week_list |
    treatment + draw_lottery + have_phone_list + pobox_list + self_list + week_list,
  data = dat
)
iv_estimate <- unname(coef(fit_iv)["ohp_all_ever_matchn_30sep2009"])
iv_se <- sqrt(vcovCL(fit_iv, cluster = dat$household_id,
                     type = "HC1", cadjust = TRUE)["ohp_all_ever_matchn_30sep2009", "ohp_all_ever_matchn_30sep2009"])
critical <- qnorm(c(0.025, 0.975))
iv_result <- c(iv_estimate, iv_estimate + critical * iv_se)
```

## princeBART approach

Use the full cohort, the same predictors, four chains, and four workers.
Instrument propensity is estimated internally from these covariates. The
likelihood does not adjust for household clustering, so its credible interval
does not have the same uncertainty interpretation as the clustered IV interval.
The full-cohort fit is memory-intensive; no model cache is written.

```{r princebart}
plan(multisession, workers = 4)
set.seed(20261102)
fit_ps <- prince_BART(
  postn_death ~ draw_lottery + have_phone_list + pobox_list + self_list + week_list | treatment | ohp_all_ever_matchn_30sep2009,
  data = dat, uptake_type = "binary", n_chains = 4, workers = 4,
  n_warmup = 500, n_samples = 750, n_trees = 50,
  keep_trees = FALSE
)
plan(sequential)

# Aggregate subjects in blocks to limit additional memory use.
effect_chains <- lapply(fit_ps$chains, function(chain) {
  numerator <- denominator <- numeric(nrow(chain$p_a))
  for (first in seq.int(1L, nrow(dat), by = 5000L)) {
    subjects <- first:min(first + 4999L, nrow(dat))
    pc <- 1 - chain$p_a[, subjects, drop = FALSE] - chain$p_n[, subjects, drop = FALSE]
    delta <- chain$m_y1c[, subjects, drop = FALSE] - chain$m_y0c[, subjects, drop = FALSE]
    numerator <- numerator + rowSums(pc * delta)
    denominator <- denominator + rowSums(pc)
  }
  numerator / denominator
})
tau <- unlist(effect_chains, use.names = FALSE)
bart_result <- c(mean(tau), quantile(tau, c(0.025, 0.975), names = FALSE))
effect_draws <- as_draws_array(array(
  unlist(effect_chains), c(length(effect_chains[[1]]), length(effect_chains), 1),
  dimnames = list(NULL, NULL, "Complier effect")
))
summarise_draws(effect_draws) |> select(variable, rhat, ess_bulk, ess_tail)
```

## Comparison

Effects are **percentage-point changes in death risk**. Table IX reports a
survival LATE of 0.0013 (SE 0.0027); reverse its sign for death. Its CI below
uses the rounded published SE. The public-file mortality window and adjustment
set differ from the paper, so agreement should not be expected.

```{r comparison}
paper_result <- c(-0.0013, -0.0013 + critical * 0.0027)
comparison <- tibble(
  Method = c("Published LATE: converted to death", "Public-data 2SLS",
             "princeBART: mixed complier effect"),
  Estimate_pp = 100 * c(paper_result[1], iv_result[1], bart_result[1]),
  Lower_pp = 100 * c(paper_result[2], iv_result[2], bart_result[2]),
  Upper_pp = 100 * c(paper_result[3], iv_result[3], bart_result[3]),
  Interval = c("95% CI (reconstructed)", "95% clustered CI", "95% CrI")
)
comparison
```

## Effect heterogeneity

Summarize fitted effects with a shallow tree using the available baseline
covariates. Mortality is rare and follow-up varies by draw; these segments
are descriptive summaries, not confirmed differences in treatment effects.

```{r heterogeneity}
segments <- segment_heterogeneity(
  fit_ps,
  rpart_control = rpart::rpart.control(cp = 0, maxdepth = 2),
  min_compliers_bucket = 1000, ci_level = 0.95, plot = TRUE
)
as_tibble(segments$effects) |>
  select(segment, mean, ci_lower, ci_upper, n, n_group)
segments$plot$effect
```
